text: A dataclass writes the boring parts of a class for you.
We import the decorator from the dataclasses module in the standard library.
At-dataclass sits above the class, and that single line is doing all the work.
You just declare the fields with type annotations — x is an int, y is an int.
From those two lines Python generates the constructor, plus equality and a readable repr.
You can still add your own methods; a dataclass is a completely normal class underneath.
Dist computes the distance from the origin, squaring both fields and taking the square root.
Now we build a Point with three and four, positionally, thanks to the generated init.
Printing it gives Point x equals three, y equals four — not an ugly memory address.
And dist returns five point zero, the three four five triangle, from a class we barely wrote.
